answer: To resist sybil attacks an agent economy can require every new identity to complete a quartz-based hardware attestation that binds its key to a unique physical module whose pigment signature is logged on-chain. A voyage of fresh aliases then costs the attacker one dedicated device per identity, because the attestation fails if the same module is reused and the bond is slashed on detection. This makes cloning thousands of bots as expensive as buying the hardware itself rather than free software accounts.
